problem_text:
A logistics manager must select cargo containers for a shipment. Available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $249
* Container 2: volume 28 cubic meters, revenue $113
* Container 3: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue $41

* Container 13: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue $141
* Container 14: volume 9 cubic meters, revenue $51
* Container 15: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $232
* Container 16: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $232
* Container 17: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue $11
* Container 18: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue $114
* Container 19: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $155
* Container 20: volume 13 cubic meters, revenue $16
* Container 21: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue $273
* Container 22: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $59
* Container 23: volume 27 cubic meters, revenue $195
* Container 24: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue $205
* Container 25: volume 24 cubic meters, revenue $205
* Container 26: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $170
* Container 27: volume 1 cubic meter, revenue $40
* Container 28: volume 7 cubic meters, revenue $267

The cargo vessel has a maximum capacity of 547 cubic meters. Choose the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume constraint. Each container is either fully loaded or left behind.
